question: Which shader-fetch patch and persistent-cache effects must a draw-entry model distinguish from dropped command words?

scope.boundary: Native-word and narrow generated-code reconciliation within the inspected scope. No complete transitive helper-write tree, no account of which code holds, replaces and releases allocator output, and no runtime model parity or safe draw-consumption result.

dependencies.use: Canonical record of accepted shader selection, copied versus persistent patch destinations and metadata contracts.
Canonical record of the separate dirty-group and bound-state inventory.
Canonical record of the device binding and shader and declaration object field evidence.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only no-analysis queries through tools/run-headless.ps1 using ghidra/DumpFunctions.java, ghidra/DumpInstructions.java and ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java; narrow exact-function generated corroboration.

inputQualification.claim: A sequential read-only mapped-memory comparison found all differences inside the historical thunk band. None overlaps the cited semantic native windows.
inputQualification.qualification: The mapped program is not byte-identical to the supported flat image. No original thunk semantics or whole-image reader absence follows. Function-body claims rely on source-equivalent inspected words; no repair was performed.

currentEvidence.decompilerLimit: Canonical decompilation truncates at Xenon save and restore thunks or undefined instructions. Sparse decoded iteration can skip gaps; it is not complete function coverage.

drawEntryGate.claim: The draw entry tests low-word mask 0x1E0000 of the dirty qword at G+0x10 before calling 0x826ADD88 with the dirty value. In the big-endian layout this mask is in G+0x14.
drawEntryGate.qualification: This groups four bits. It does not assign each bit the same semantic action.

modeBoundary.claim: The entry masks this bit and conditionally calls 0x826AC6C8. That helper writes derived G+0x2940 and device-byte state plus command words.
modeBoundary.qualification: Complete helper effects and original semantic names remain qualified.

modeBoundary.claim: A shader and fetch update arm can select a persistent variant through 0x826ADC48 or an allocated command copy through 0x826ADA38, with metadata loading through 0x826ADB98.
modeBoundary.qualification: Actual selected variant, cache compatibility, helper returns and allocation remain guarded.

modeBoundary.claim: The generated path, within the inspected scope, includes separate pixel and alternate selection and derived mode state; it is not interchangeable with the stride-triggered patch arm.
modeBoundary.qualification: This is generated corroboration of the native windows, not runtime activation.

modeBoundary.claim: The bit reaches ADD88 through the draw-entry grouped check. With input exactly 0x40000 and no locally added 0x80000 or 0x100000, it skips the 0x20000 helper and the 0x180000 grouped stores at 0x826AE20C and 0x826AE21C. A39F8 still clears G+0x10 at 0x826A3B44.
modeBoundary.qualification: Other ADD88 mode, binding and command conditions still depend on device state. No independent action was assigned to this bit; do not infer a no-op or map it to 0x20000.

transientStrideBoundary.claim: The selected UP lowerer and sink path temporarily stores the low byte of input stride in dwords at G+0x30F0 and can set dirty mask 0x80000 when it differs from the cached stride and a vertex shader is bound.
transientStrideBoundary.qualification: The transient value, restored exit byte, later dirty clears and side-buffer protocol are distinct outputs.

patcherBoundary.claim: The patcher derives three-word, 12-byte fetch-instruction records using shader patch metadata, a 12-byte declaration-record scan and stream stride bytes, orders and canonicalizes scratch records, then copies selected records to codeDestination+12*index.
patcherBoundary.qualification: The guarded byte transformation, table and seed result, scratch ordering and selected 12-byte copy effect are recorded in the byte contract. Whether the actual input and table stay unchanged, bounds, aliases, and which code holds, replaces and releases the caller resource remain required. This is not a complete host draw model. Ordering and canonicalization write stack scratch.

allocatedCopy.claim: Passes the allocated and copied command-code buffer to 0x826AD150, with VS, declaration, stride bytes and variant supplied separately.
allocatedCopy.qualification: This does not imply that only a disposable copy can be modified. Allocator output, and which code holds, replaces and releases it, are not yet established.

persistentResource.claim: Can pass the shader resource's selected code address to the same patcher before publishing cache fields.
persistentResource.publication: The selected ADD88 branch appends header 0xC0012701, an encoded address derived from the same C+load32(M_v) patched by ADC48, and load32(M_v+4)>>2. It then stamps the selected record. The address encoding is (D&0x1FFFFFFF)+(((rol32(D,12)&0xFFF)+512)&0x1000).
persistentResource.packetInterpretation: External Xenia Type3Opcode identifies 0x27 as pointer-based IM_LOAD and 0x2B as IM_LOAD_IMMEDIATE: https://github.com/xenia-project/xenia/blob/95a5c3ee250f80c3b9d139658649d9ffb6db3eec/src/xenia/gpu/xenos.h#L1523-L1525 . ADB98's 0x2F packet is an ALU-constant load, not the shader-code byte writer.
persistentResource.qualification: The preserved code allocation is the published instruction-memory input under that packet and address interpretation. Actual GPU fetch, cache visibility, pointer and variant validity, which code holds, replaces and releases the allocation, and fence guards remain unobserved. A CPU reader of the selected patched guest range sees its changed bytes under the byte contract's guards on whether values stay unchanged and on aliases.

interiorSite.claim: This is an interior linked-call site for 0x826ADB98, not an independently identified shader-loader entry.

shaderConstructionBoundary.notation: B is the compiled input blob; under retained fields M=load32(B+4), S=load32(B+8). VS and C are the two selected allocation returns.
shaderConstructionBoundary.allocationRequests: CreateVS requests M+40+((load32(B)&1)?832:0) bytes for VS and S bytes separately for C through 0x82E29168. The metadata helper call 0x8269467C requests 0x8281ABB8(VS+872,B,M); call 0x826946B0 requests 0x827F8550(C,B+M,S).
shaderConstructionBoundary.codePointer: Init receives(VS,C) at 0x826946BC and stores C at VS+32 at 0x82692B78. This is the preserved separate code allocation, not VS itself.
shaderConstructionBoundary.metadata: Init reads offsets at VS+896+8*v. Their producer is the metadata transfer request, corresponding to blob B+24+8*v if that transfer completes as requested. Init does not synthesize this table. It forms M_v=VS+load32(VS+896+8*v)+872 and code=C+load32(M_v).
shaderConstructionBoundary.savedRecords: For selected patch-list word P_i, init copies 12 bytes from code+12*(P_i&0xFFF) to VS+68+416*v+12*i when the addresses differ. It stores -1 at VS+40+416*v at 0x82692C30; that store is a cache tag, not an offset-table write.
shaderConstructionBoundary.corroboration: Canonical rerevved generated/default/rerevved_recomp.119.cpp:12769-12939 and rerevved_recomp.199.cpp:12503-12648 at observed HEAD81798450751cfb75460269f82c2eb4df02754e80.
shaderConstructionBoundary.qualification: These are allocation and transfer requests and direct pointer and record stores. The metadataTransferBoundary supplies a relation for N>=16 transfers and returns that holds only under its stated premises, including its aligned source envelope, destination and stack extent, alias, execution and value-preservation premises. Hook effects, actual extents, which code holds, replaces and releases the allocator output, blob and metadata validity and aliases remain guarded; the separate code-copy request remains outside that relation.

metadataTransferBoundary.evidenceClass: Static relation that holds only under its stated premises, with separately identified generated corroboration; no runtime transfer observation.
metadataTransferBoundary.request: CreateVS 0x826945E8 call 0x8269467C requests 0x8281ABB8(D,S,N), D=VS+872,S=B,N=M=load32(B+4). The separate 0x827F8550 code request remains outside this transfer relation.
metadataTransferBoundary.supportedDomain: N>=16, zero-extended 32-bit N, SP and LR, nonwrapping valid guest extents; SP 16-byte aligned. Source data-load envelope R=[floor16(S),ceil16(S+N)) is readable; W=[D,D+N) is writable. R,W and the listed stack footprint have no interfering physical aliases; R and W are disjoint. Inputs, mappings, source bytes, scratch and save slots remain stable. All scalar, vector, partial-store, cache and ABI leaves execute with the inspected semantics and return normally, without trapping or replacement-hook differences. Actual B alignment is unrestricted and unobserved.
metadataTransferBoundary.relation: On this domain, post[D+i]=pre[S+i] for 0<=i<N. Parent return at 0x8281AE8C supplies original incoming r3 in full64 bits; its low32 is D. CreateVS overwrites this return while forming its next allocation request.
metadataTransferBoundary.alignmentAndLength: For N>=16 define p=(-D)&0xF, a=(-D)&0x7F, q=min(a>>4,(N-p)>>4), A=p+16*q, K=128*floor((N-A)/128), T=N-A-K. Prefix 0x8281ACC0..ACDC writes p bytes, then 0x8281AD44..AD60 transfers q 16-byte chunks. If K>0, D+A is 128-byte aligned. Source low 4 bits at 0x8281AD68 and AD74 select aligned parent bulk or 0x82825410(D+A,S+A,K) at 0x8281AE20. Remaining T bytes use full 16-byte and final partial tails at 0x8281AE38..AE88. Lengths sum exactly to N.
metadataTransferBoundary.dataFootprint: Source vector loads cover R, including up to 15 bytes before S and up to 15 after S+N. Destination data stores cover exactly W. In addition, 0x8281AD1C zeroes the first complete 128-byte bulk line when K>=128; aligned 0x8281ADB8 zeroes the next line when remaining>256, while unaligned 0x82825448 does so when remaining>=256. These intermediate zero writes are subsets of W and are overwritten on normal completion. They preclude an unrestricted overlap guarantee.
metadataTransferBoundary.cacheTouches: 0x8281ACA4 requests S+128*j for 0<=128*j<min(N,1024). Bulk 0x8281ADA8 and helper 0x82825444 request currentSource+1024 when remaining>1024. Each EA lies within the requested source span; its 128-byte cache line may extend beyond R. Supported cache-touch semantics and any required line address validity are premises, distinct from the data-load footprint.
metadataTransferBoundary.stackAndReturn: For incoming SP, save26 writes and restore26 reads six full64 GPR slots at [SP-56,SP-8) and 4-byte LR at [SP-8,SP-4). Parent writes 4-byte backchain [SP-176,SP-172) and 16-byte vector mask [SP-80,SP-64), reloading the latter after the unaligned helper, including K=0. Parent restores full64 r26..31, retaining CreateVS live r27=M,r28=B+M,r29=code size,r30=VS,r31=B. LR restoration zero-extends the saved low32 bits; it is not claimed that arbitrary high64 LR bits stay unchanged. Volatile GPRs 0, 3..12, CTR, XER, CR0, CR6, CR7 and used vectors are not preserved by this contract.

continuations.0x827F89D8: Scalar leaf uses at most three leading bytes to align the destination to 4 bytes, aligned word loads or four byte loads per word, then 0..3 trailing bytes. Valid nonwrapping disjoint requested spans suffice without extra aligned reads; r3 remains the original full64 destination. Parent reaches it only on N<16 in the inspected body.
continuations.0x82825410: For its selected K multiple of 128 and 128-byte-aligned destination, copies K bytes using aligned 16-byte source loads and permutations; helper r3 and r4 advance by K and r5 becomes 0. K=0 returns immediately without a data load or store. Parent discards this local return and restores its own original destination.

metadataTransferBoundary.smallLengthStop: N<16 is excluded. The parent's residual byte loop subtracts the live word loaded from 0x82F2FA74 at 0x8281AC50; its value and termination are not established here. The scalar leaf alone does not close this parent path, which can also use an 8-byte load or store.
metadataTransferBoundary.metadataJoin: Subject to completed transfer,28+8*v<=M, valid downstream table bounds and preservation through intervening allocation, code-copy and init, load32(VS+896+8*v)=preload32(B+24+8*v). This narrows metadata-copy qualification without proving a current shader or asset identity, code-copy delivery or shader semantic equivalence.
metadataTransferBoundary.allocationQualification: The accepted VS request is M+40+((load32(B)&1)?832:0). Without size arithmetic wrap, bit 0 = 1 requests M+872 and covers the requested metadata endpoint. Bit 0 = 0 requests M+40 and does not alone establish backing through VS+872+M. Actual writable extent remains a premise; no defect or larger allocator backing is inferred for excluded inputs.

nativeEvidence.method: Foreground read-only ghidra/DumpFunctions.java and ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java, with every selected native word compared to the supported flat image identified by image.json.
nativeEvidence.result: All selected words matched the supported flat image. Canonical parent decompilation remained thunk-truncated; VMX128 interpretation used the separately hashed exact generated functions, with execution semantics holding only under the stated premises. No whole-program byte identity is claimed.

metadataTransferBoundary.generatedQualification: These are separately hashed generated artifacts from the canonical title checkout, independently of native-worktree handwritten source inspected by Git object. No source-to-generation byte-identity claim ties them to the title source revision or the earlier generatedRevision. Native words establish current-image identity; generated windows corroborate interpretation.
metadataTransferBoundary.falsifier: A supported accepted input with a wrong requested byte, a data load beyond R, a store beyond W plus the stated stack footprint, a zero line outside W, a changed saved caller-live GPR, or failure to return under the explicit execution premises. Unsupported or trapping vector forms or different hook behavior require their exact route or implementation discriminator; first selected VMX128 check is 0x8281ACC0 for p>0 or 0x8281AD38 for p=0. Runtime support and trapping were not observed.

dirtyProducerBoundary.encodingSearch: Aligned initialized mapped words: oris immediates 4, 8 and 16 followed within four words by stw+0x14 or std+0x10 using the same result register. 29 raw pairs, cap128 not reached; intervening writes and base provenance required confirmation.

producers.condition: Direct render-state setter; also changes G+0x293C bit 3 and ORs low-word bit 0x200.

SetStreamSource stores stride byte at G+0x30F0+stream. It sets the patch bit when unsigned(stride>>2) is nonzero and differs from the byte at G+0x2E38+stream. This is separate from its caller-mask OR into G+0x18, not a mask transfer.
Selected render-target path with index 0, nonnull input object and selected type nibble 5, 7 or 15; helper and object validity remain guarded.
Selected initialization path ORs the two bits separately. Its earlier 0x82692344 candidate stores to G+0x20 instead.
On the reached hook, count and limit path; complete helper effects remain qualified.
Reached hook-guarded path; earlier 0x82698A08 candidate stores to G+0x20 instead.
Reached Resolve path after its helper branch merge point; 0x8269EF2C stores to G+0x20 instead.
Reached clear-quad path after earlier object and mask guards; 0x826A27E8 stores to G+0x20 instead.

dirtyProducerBoundary.existingProducers: The runtime-surface evidence is the canonical record of SetPixelShader 0x82692948, SetVertexShader 0x82692C48, SetVertexDeclaration 0x82692E60 and SetFVF 0x826946D8. The UP stride sites remain under transientStrideBoundary.
dirtyProducerBoundary.qualification: This is a producer matrix limited to the eight functions read, not every API or encoding. Remaining 0x826B1DA0 candidates exceed this eight-function read set. Computed masks, other distances, indexed and bulk stores, helper aliases and runtime activation are not yet established.

bitActionStoreBoundary.claim: With a live G+0x3198 binding, mode logic can write G+0x2954 and +0x2884 and add local dirty bits. The 0x100000 arm additionally reaches guarded metadata and cursor and G+0x2928 writes. The 0x180000 grouped test at 0x826AE1F0..0x826AE1FC controls the G+0x2924 and +0x2920 stores at 0x826AE20C and 0x826AE21C.
bitActionStoreBoundary.commandBoundary: Subsequent G+0x2ABC bit 0x40, local-mask and record guards select ring append blocks, record stamps and cursor publication. cpuVisibleDeviceWrites and fenceBoundary hold the canonical record of their exact stores.
bitActionStoreBoundary.qualification: The direct branch and store results leave open the effects of metadata, allocation, ring-wrap and other helpers. It does not assign the 0x40000 bit an independent shader operation.

fetchFieldInterpretation.locator: VertexFetchInstruction::Data; bits numbered from each 32-bit word's least significant bit.
fetchFieldInterpretation.word0: Bits20..24 bank,25..26 selector,27..29 prefetch. The reference computes fetch-constant index as3*bank+selector.
fetchFieldInterpretation.word1: Bits0..11 destination swizzle,12 signedness,13 integer/normalization mode,16..21 data format,30 mini-fetch mode.
fetchFieldInterpretation.word2: Bits0..7 dword stride,8..30 signed dword offset.
fetchFieldInterpretation.qualification: External decoder interpretation corroborates the native byte masks; it is not title or hardware proof. The transformation also changes swizzle, signedness, normalization, prefetch and full and mini selection. Sorting moves entire records, so a fixed destination may receive other source-record bits. No opcode validation of every selected input was established; require valid vfetch metadata.

persistentCacheBoundary.claim: The compatibility key is declaration VD+0x30, not the command cursor or a device tag. A zero declaration tag can allocate an ID using global counter 0x82FA0544. The selected record stores a tag at +0x28 and stride qwords at +0x30 and +0x38, and the device caches stride state at G+0x2E38 and +0x2E40.
persistentCacheBoundary.qualification: A compatible cache hit can reuse code without running the patcher. A busy variant can reject persistent patching. A host model must preserve these distinct branches.

compatibleCacheHitSubmodel.conditions: The selected record's +0x28 tag equals VD+0x30 and the OR of both 64-bit masked stride differences is zero.
compatibleCacheHitSubmodel.outputs: Copy current G+0x30F0 and G+0x30F8 to G+0x2E38 and G+0x2E40, then return r3=1.
compatibleCacheHitSubmodel.qualification: This arm skips the patcher, declaration ID allocation, record tag and stride stores and fence test. It is a limited persistent-output model for this callee, not the complete register and frame contract or a draw-entry consume model.

fenceBoundary.claim: Selected variant records receive current G+0x2A9C at record+0x40 after selected program publication paths. The persistent selector compares this stamp against completion state reached through G+0x2A90.
fenceBoundary.qualification: These are CPU-visible reuse and lifetime inputs. Dropping command words does not alone justify dropping stamps.

cpuVisibleDeviceWrites.claim: Mode, shader selection, shadow-register, byte-flag and cursor stores are distinct from dynamic command-buffer payload words.
cpuVisibleDeviceWrites.qualification: The list is a direct-store result within the inspected scope, not all transitive helper writes or an exhaustive reader classification.

dirtyClears.claim: The selected draw body clears dirty qwords at G+0x0,+0x8,+0x10,+0x18,+0x20 after their respective helper paths. A consume's dirty-word policy is a separate model decision, not evidence that native writes are absent.

guards: Do not call the shader update ring-only: persistent shader bytes, declaration tags, variant cache fields and fence stamps can be CPU-visible outputs.
Do not execute a patch on a cache-hit branch that native code reuses without patching.
Do not infer a complete draw-entry model from a one-record patcher formula.
Do not infer actual stream and declaration identity, bounds, lifetime or nonaliasing from compatible shapes.
No full coverage of the call tree, allocator, synchronization or runtime parity was established.
nextDiscriminators: Identify the actual 0x80000 variant path and its declaration tag, stride masks, completion window and current code destination before selecting a host-model case.
Identify whether the byte contract's current input and table stay unchanged, the protected stack and selected code-range guards before accepting a caller case or claiming runtime parity.
Keep zero-tag global-ID allocation, busy-variant fallback, allocation and ring-wrap and unresolved far-helper paths refused until their effects are separately established.

A separately authorized exit probe must predict without mutating entry state, run Original once, then compare all modeled device, cache and declaration fields and every changed shader byte; classify command-only differences separately.
conclusion: The dirty vertex-fetch path can patch preserved shader-code allocation bytes as well as allocated command copies and writes CPU-visible cache, tag, shadow and fence state. A translator using unpatched code and current declaration and stride state is not disproved by those byte differences, but its GPU semantic equivalence and complete guest exit parity are not established. Shared-ID allocation, completion, allocator, aliases, metadata validity and helper effects remain qualified; no complete safe consume model is established.
